articles.title: Re: NHS staff warned they could face prison if they inappropriately access patient data
articles.description: Agreement: I Agree Body: Dear Editor The warning given by Sir Jim Mackey to sack the NHS staff that fail to recognise the rights of patients to respect is correct. Patient medical records are private, highly personal and should remain confidential. It is unfortunate that the UK Government does not expect such standards for itself. The drive by politicians to create a biotechnology industry to boost the economy is based on the use of these very same patient records obtained by presumed consent, which does not require active consent.[1] Assurances that pseudonymisation will protect the privacy is undermined by the recognition of cybercrime and human errors.[2] The failure to respect the health records is further exemplified by the discovery that Palantir could directly access the patient records.[3] Such double standard is highly regrettable. Their failure to act ethically might well encourage other examples of disrespect to the medical information donated altruistically to biobanks such as Our Future Health and the UK Biobank to continue.
